title: Graph Neural Networks with Node-wise Architecture

problem.claim: A single GNN architecture applied equally to all nodes may be insufficient for diverse local graph patterns.

gap.claim: Node-wise architecture search faces scalability challenges and must determine architectures for test nodes.

contributions.claim: A framework uses parametric controllers to determine each node's GNN architecture from its local patterns.
The framework instantiates depth, aggregator, and resolution controllers and trains them cooperatively with a backbone GNN.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Performance improvements are attributed to the depth, aggregator, and resolution controllers, respectively.
The proposed framework significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods on five of ten real-world datasets.
The authors report that node-wise architecture helps GNNs become versatile models.

narrative_sequence.summary: NAS for GNNs seeks an architecture for a new graph.
Applying one architecture uniformly may not handle diverse node-level patterns.
Node-wise search is difficult because naive per-node NAS is not scalable and test-node architectures must be determined.
Parametric controllers select node-specific architectures from local patterns and cooperate with a backbone GNN.
The abstract reports controller-related improvements and stronger results on five of ten real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: Uniform architecture choices may be inadequate when local patterns vary across nodes.

interpretation.claim: Model capacity or computation may need to adapt to local structural variation.

application.claim: Consider instance- or node-conditioned architecture selection when graph heterogeneity is consequential.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that node-wise architecture improves every dataset or graph setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or numerical performance results.
The abstract does not describe controller architectures, training objectives, computational costs, or scalability measurements.
The abstract does not provide independent verification or full experimental details.
